current_available_skills.name: browser-use
current_available_skills.description: Control a real browser to navigate pages, click, type, fill forms, inspect rendered UI, take screenshots, or record video. Load only when the user asks to open or automate a browser, interact with or test rendered page UI, scrape a site that needs browser execution, or capture a browser screenshot or video. Do not load for backend logs, traces, API or stream events, source-code inspection, or plain HTTP or web research that does not require a browser.

current_available_skills.name: Context Doctor
current_available_skills.description: Investigate and repair an agent's context — memory, system prompt, and skills — using observed behavior as evidence. Use when the user asks to audit, clean up, or fix your memory or context, or runs /tmp/x/doctor. Do not load for routine memory reads or edits, or requests that merely mention memory.

current_available_skills.name: creating-mods
current_available_skills.description: Creates and edits trusted local Haruyuki mods, including tools, slash commands, local-only model providers, lifecycle/turn events, scoped conversation helpers, panels, and capability-gated behavior. Use when asked to make a mod, add an agent-callable tool, add a slash command, add a local provider/model adapter, transform turns, react to app events, or add lightweight mod UI outside the dedicated /tmp/x/statusline flow.

current_available_skills.name: creating-skills
current_available_skills.description: Guide for creating effective skills. This skill should be used when users want to create a new skill (or update an existing skill) that extends Haruyuki's capabilities with specialized knowledge, workflows, or tool integrations.

current_available_skills.name: curating-memory-palace
current_available_skills.description: Rules for the Memory Palace (palace/), the view on your Memory page in the Letta dashboard that shows the user where things stand, what you could do next, and how to make you more useful. Load it before creating or editing anything in palace/, when a message starts with "Palace action:" or "Palace reply on", and, when palace/ exists, whenever you notice a blocker, a decision for the user, work you could offer, or a routine that started, broke, or changed.

current_available_skills.name: customizing-commands
current_available_skills.description: Creates, edits, and enables Haruyuki mod-provided slash commands. Use when the user asks to add a custom /tmp/x/command, slash command, command shortcut, scoped conversation-backed command, or command-driven panel behavior.

current_available_skills.name: customizing-statusline
current_available_skills.description: Creates, edits, and migrates Haruyuki statusline mods. Use when handling the /tmp/x/statusline command or continuing work started by /tmp/x/statusline.

current_available_skills.name: editing-letta-code-desktop-preferences
current_available_skills.description: Edits Haruyuki Desktop (LCD) preferences by safely reading and updating ~/tmp/x/desktop_preferences.json. Use only when the user asks to change current Desktop/LCD settings such as theme, default working directory, remote access preference, or remote environment name via the preferences JSON.

current_available_skills.name: finding-agents
current_available_skills.description: Find other agents on the same server. Use when the user asks about other agents, wants to migrate memory from another agent, or needs to find an agent by name or tags.

current_available_skills.name: haruyuki-guide
current_available_skills.description: Answer questions about this build from the reference documents bundled with it. Load before answering anything about commands, flags, slash commands, settings keys, file layout, or agent behavior — and never answer those from memory.

current_available_skills.name: initializing-memory
current_available_skills.description: Comprehensive guide for initializing or reorganizing agent memory. Load this skill when running /tmp/x/init, when the user asks you to set up your memory, or when you need guidance on creating effective memory files.

current_available_skills.name: messaging-agents
current_available_skills.description: Send a message to another haruyuki agent, continue a thread with one, check on it, or reply to a message another agent sent you. Use when you need to ask, inform, or coordinate with another agent, or when a message from another agent arrives.

current_available_skills.name: migrating-memory
current_available_skills.description: Migrate memory blocks from an existing agent to the current agent. Use when the user wants to copy or share memory from another agent, or during /tmp/x/init when setting up a new agent that should inherit memory from an existing one.

current_available_skills.name: scheduling-tasks
current_available_skills.description: Manage resident scheduled tasks through the /tmp/x/schedule hub and the haruyuki cron CLI — conversation targets, permission tiers, catch-up, autostart, storage, and run history. Use Wake for an ordinary self-bound reminder in the current conversation.

current_available_skills.name: self-configuration
current_available_skills.description: Inspect or modify Haruyuki's own memory, model, context window, system prompt, compaction, permissions, toolsets, mods, skills, channels, schedules, agent secrets, and local runtime settings. Use when the user asks how this agent or conversation is configured, asks about account usage, remaining credits, or model quota, asks you to change how you behave or how the harness runs you, or renames you.

current_available_skills.name: syncing-memory-filesystem
current_available_skills.description: Diagnose and repair MemFS repository setup, checkout problems, optional backup remotes, or merge/rebase conflicts. Do not load for routine memory reads or edits.

current_available_skills.name: using-mcp-tools
current_available_skills.description: Reference for the `haruyuki mcp` CLI, which finds and invokes MCP tools available to this agent. A system reminder already lists your connected MCP servers and the basic search/schema/call commands; invoke this skill when you need more — browsing a server's tools, passing large or file-based arguments, tuning search, or troubleshooting missing servers, tools, and errors.

current_available_skills.name: workflow-authoring
current_available_skills.description: Reference for writing a Workflow tool script (script API and gotchas, pipeline-vs-barrier rules, quality patterns, worked examples). Load before authoring a script for a workflow the user already opted into; it does not itself authorize running one.

## 未决与后续
Nothing is unfinished. The sole request was the one-word reply "ok", which was answered; no follow-up task has been given yet.

## 错误与修正
No approaches were tried, so none failed or were ruled out. Note the environment caveat for later work: HEREDOC syntax does not work on this Windows shell, and native stderr redirection in PowerShell 5.1 can turn benign warnings into exit code 1.

## 关系与情绪线
No relationship movement in this conversation; it is a fresh, essentially contentless session consisting of a system environment notice and a single trivial instruction. The tone so far is neutral and untested.

## 记忆文件索引
Memory directory: C:/work/memory — no files created or consulted in this conversation. Working directory: C:/work/work (not a git repository).

## 故事梗概
This is the barest possible conversation: one injected message and one word of instruction. The injected message is a Haruyuki execution-environment notice stating the local time (Saturday, 2026-11-14, 20:59 GMT+8), that the machine is Windows running Haruyuki 0.6.0, that the working directory is a temporary haruyuki-record scratch folder with no git repository, and that the conversation is connected to a Haruyuki execution environment. It also carries the practical shell notes for this host: the detected shell is a bundled niu.exe reached through the .dsh/dsh-ops path, Unix-style shell syntax should be used, HEREDOC syntax does not work, and PowerShell 5.1 will not tolerate native stderr redirection because it converts benign warnings into exit codes. Nothing in that notice required action; it is context, not a task.

The only user turn asked for exactly one word: "ok". There was no work to do, no question to answer, no bug to chase, no design to weigh. The reply was that single word, and the conversation ends there. There is no arc to describe, no mood that turned, and no fork in any road — the transcript is a system notice followed by a compliance test of formatting discipline. The whole content of what happened is that an instruction about brevity was followed literally, with no embellishment, no explanation, and no attempt to be helpful beyond the letter of the request.

What is worth carrying forward is only context, not substance. First, the environment facts, so a future turn does not have to rediscover them: Windows host, temporary working directory that is not a git repo, the bundled niu.exe shell, and the two shell caveats (no heredocs, avoid native stderr redirection in PowerShell). Second, the fact that nothing has actually been asked yet, so any later request arrives cold and the relationship is at its starting point. If the conversation continues, the next message will be the real beginning; everything before it is preamble.

The conversation could be archived in a single line without losing anything of consequence. It is recorded in this detail only so that the continuity record is complete and honest rather than padded with invented substance: nothing open, nothing ruled out, no relational movement, and a memory index that names the directory and working folder without claiming any files exist inside them yet.
